title: Multipart invoke responses wrap arrays in envelope causing structured-output parsers to fail
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported that function/tool invocation responses emitted in streaming/multipart mode sometimes arrive wrapped inside an additional envelope object that contains metadata delimiters. Our structured-output parser (used for tool JSON extraction and typed outputs) fails to locate the expected array/object root, leading to downstream parse errors and application-level exceptions. The issue is observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but manifests more frequently when streaming is enabled and when a proxy layer injects headers/boundary markers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Enable streaming/multipart response on any model route that supports tool/function calls
2) Configure a proxy that inserts multipart boundaries or transforms response envelopes (common in customer private deployments)
3) Invoke a function that returns structured JSON array or typed object as the final tool output
4) Observe parser error: expected root array/object not found; runtime throws ParserError: Unexpected token at position 0
mitigation: Short term: disable streaming/multipart for affected customer routes (config toggle applied for three customers on 2026-03-02)
Fallback: route-through relaxed parser that attempts to unwrap common envelope keys (payload, envelope, body) before structured extraction
Customer guidance: advise customers using custom proxies to preserve raw application/json responses and avoid inserting multipart markers
root_cause: A recent change in streaming framing logic (runtime commit runtime@c3f4e) added a generic multipart framing wrapper to support mixed media tool outputs. In edge cases where downstream proxies re-encoded or concatenated chunks, the wrapper nested the actual JSON payload inside an envelope object instead of emitting the payload root at top-level. The structured-output parser assumed top-level payload schemas and did not include robust envelope unwrapping heuristics.
proposed_fix: Primary: enhance structured-output parser to detect and unwrap common envelope patterns (keys: payload, envelope, body, data) and re-validate against expected schema before failing
Secondary: make streaming framing idempotent to avoid double-wrapping when proxies re-emit boundaries
Support: add strict/relaxed parsing modes configurable per-route with safe defaults for Hosted customers
customer_escalations: Zendesk#100234 - EnterprisePayments: production explorer throws ParserError on tool response (priority: outage)
Zendesk#100289 - MedDataAI: private appliance returns wrapped tool payloads causing downstream deserialization failures

timeline: 2026-03-01: First customer report (EnterprisePayments) - initial triage by SE
2026-03-02: Applied emergency toggle to disable streaming for affected Hosted routes; created mitigation relaxed-parser proxy for EnterprisePayments
2026-03-03: Repro validated in Dedicated staging with synthetic proxy that inserts boundaries
2026-03-04: Root cause traced to streaming framing change in runtime commit c3f4e; draft fix proposed
2026-03-06: Code + tests submitted (PR 9241); security review requested
2026-03-08: QA found regression where unwrapping introduced false positives on legitimately nested schemas; iteration 2 in progress
2026-03-10: Release candidate built and scheduled for canary on 2026-03-11
decision_log: Decision 2026-03-02: Immediately disable streaming for high-impact customers to stop new failures (approved by Ops and PM)
Decision 2026-03-05: Implement parser-side unwrapping rather than changing customer proxies to avoid breaking external integrations (approved by Eng Lead Lena Müller)
Decision 2026-03-07: Add opt-in relaxed parsing on route config to allow stricter enforcement for security-sensitive tenants (approved by Security)
Decision 2026-03-09: Require additional integration tests with proxy-rewrite scenarios before broad rollout
deployment_plan: Canary 1 (2026-03-11): runtime-2.5.1-rc on 10% of Hosted traffic (non-critical routes)
Canary 2 (2026-03-12): runtime-2.5.1-rc on 30% with Dedicated staging mirrors
Full rollout (2026-03-13-2026-03-15): gradual increase to 100% pending error rate < 0.1% over 4h windows
Private customers: provide hotfix patch and configuration guide; coordinate with field SEs for appliance upgrades
rollback_plan: If post-deploy error rate > 1% or customer regressions reported, revert runtime to previous stable (runtime-2.5.0) and re-enable per-route streaming disable toggles. Run emergency postmortem and notify affected customers.
qa_notes: Unit: add envelope-detection tests for keys: payload/envelope/body/data and for string-escaped JSON payloads
Integration: simulate proxy insertion of multipart headers and validate parser unwrap and schema validation
E2E: deploy to staging with a consumer app that expects typed array output and verify no behavioural change on valid inputs
Performance: verify unwrapping cost < 0.15ms per request at p95 under 5000qps sampling
next_steps: Finish iteration on PR 9241 to avoid false-positive unwrapping edgecases (owner: Daniel Park)
Add integration tests that mirror customer proxy behavior and include them in the CI matrix
Coordinate with Support to schedule Private appliance patch windows for customers who already experienced failures
Publish runbook entry: how to safely toggle streaming per-route and when to use relaxed parsing mode
